title: First Day Covered by an Assisted Living Care Level Increase
content:
Under the Assisted Living Residency and Care Agreement, the first day covered by the level-increase charge follows the kind of reassessment and the timeliness of the written level notice. The reassessment is the latest assessment on the residency; the notice is the most recent written level notice.

| Reassessment that found the increase | Written level notice | First day covered |
|---|---|---|
| Routine or post-move-in | — | The notice date plus 30 calendar days |
| Change-of-condition or post-hospital | Issued more than 2 calendar days after the assessment date | The notice date |
| Change-of-condition or post-hospital | Issued on time, no more than 2 calendar days after the assessment date | The assessment date |

The days covered then run from the first day covered through the last day of the billing month of the most recent full-month care fee charge, both days counted; where the first day covered falls after that last day, no day is covered.

The first day covered governs what the level-increase charge bills even where the level's recorded effective date is earlier, so the new level's monthly care fee is billed only from that day; the care level the residency carries and the level stated on the written notice are not changed by it.

### Both sides of the timeliness threshold (hypothetical change-of-condition reassessment on 10 June, June billed in full)

| Notice issued | Days after the assessment | First day covered | Days covered in June |
|---|---|---|---|
| 12 June | 2 — on time | 10 June | 21 |
| 13 June | 3 — late | 13 June | 18 |

### Routine or post-move-in increase (hypothetical)

- Notice issued 20 April: first day covered 20 May; with May billed in full, days covered 20 May through 31 May, that is 12.
- Notice issued 5 June: first day covered 5 July, after the last day of June; with June the month billed in full, no day is covered.
